chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: Ali (peace be upon him) said:
A woman has ten 'awrat (parts to be covered/veiled). When she marries, one of them is covered for her; and when she dies, all of her 'awrat are covered.

key_terms.عَوْرَة: A part of the body that must be covered or veiled; modesty zone

ai.seo_question: What are the ten awrat of a woman according to Imam Ali (a.s.) and how do marriage and death affect them?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) outlines a dynamic jurisprudence of modesty, noting that while a woman possesses ten 'awrat' (parts requiring covering), marriage alleviates the requirement for one part, and death restores full coverage. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that the scope of *awrah* is not static but shifts according to the woman's social and legal status, balancing public modesty with private intimacy. The hadith underscores the dignity of the female form, where marriage serves as a sanctified veil for specific aspects of the body, while death returns the body to its complete state of modesty.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-116 According to the same documentation, Ali (a.s.) said, “
A woman has ten things to cover up. Once she marries she has covered up one and once she dies she has covered up all ten.”
